comment: Bike the first part!!
Get the bike & bring more water than you think you need especially on a hot day

I'd wanted to do this hike for many years, and it was well worth the wait! The views were amazing, the trail was well cared for, and it was such a beautiful day. There are a few sections that are very steep, and some of the stairs going up are a bit loose. One section has very rocky terrain, and it was the most precarious of the day, but once you pass it its smooth sailing. Definitely a hard trail though, make sure to bring enough water and food for several hours.

Breathtaking views, well worth the long trek. Mostly not too tough, aside from the short but steep climb, which is made much easier by a series of stairs. We went on a hot sunny day in late July, and the swarms of flies at the viewpoints at the top were almost unbearable. Still worth it!

Bucket list hike off the list. Amazing hike. Hardest hike I ever did too. The views were absolutely stunning. And soooo worth it. 
Bring plenty of water and energy snacks. 
You will need them.

This beautiful hike kicked my behind!! That last stretch from the junction to the car was definitely a struggle lol. 

Bring as much water as you think you’ll need for 6-8 hours and then double it. Also bring bug spray!! My phone also died 3/4 of the way through, so I couldn’t properly track the hike on here, so that is definitely something to keep in mind. 

I recommend starting at 7am(ish) if you want to avoid doing the climax of the incline/decline directly in the sun. 

Overall, one of my favourite hikes of all time!! There are many, many gorgeous viewpoints and sights to see along the way.
Extremely flat to start then you get all 1900 feet of elevation in about a mile and a half! Fun hike with great views of Lake Superior and Isle Royale.  BUG SPRAY MANDATORY
Bring a bike, the first and last 6.5km are bike able with only a few sections we chose to walk. Bike racks are available when the terrain changes to longer be bike able.

Fantastic hike, but long. Was able to do it with my 9 year old. We biked the first part and loved having hiking poles for the climb up. Well maintained trail but not easy. The most bugs on the trail…bug spray was useless. The views were crazy beautiful.
Beautiful views but really tough at parts near the top. Bring a bike to save time!!! (I didn't do this and regretted it)
Bring your bike.. 😍

Amazing views, steep hike take good amount of breaks and water with you.

Views are worth it
It worth it

Easy for the first few km then a steep climb over a relatively short distance makes this hike a good challenge. Bring bug spray!!!  The views at the top were great. Took 6:30 to do including lunch at the top.

Well kept and clear paths. The mosquitos were awful!!!

Amazing view at the end! It was all worth it!
Lots of skeeters! Biked 10 miles and hiked 4
Very muddy and buggy. Bring a can of spray to smack the mosquitoes, because they were laughing at off.
Buggy and muddy. Other than that it was a great hike! Biked the first and last 7k and hiked the middle section!

We completed the hike in just over 6 hours without bikes. The trail is fairly flat and easy for the first 7 km, then turns into a steep, strenuous climb. We’re only occasional hikers and still found it manageable.
There were a couple of turns near the top where we had to check our map, but overall the trail is easy to follow. The hardest part for us was the last 7km,  bringing bikes would have definitely saved us a lot of time and effort. Bathrooms are available along the way.
Very buggy, but with mosquito nets and bug spray, we were fine.
Overall a challenging hike but definitely worth it!! Beautiful trail and views.
Best to bike in, park bike and then climb.

We completed this hike under 8 hours. We started at around 8:40 am - finished around 4:30pm.

The first portion was mainly flat surfaced. It was a nice walk in the woods. We also stopped on the way to see the Sea Lion lookout, which added an additional KM to our route. 

Some bathrooms on the way & back country campsites too. 

Approached the first portion of the stairs, where you can lock your bikes; which we wished we had of brought some as the walk back was pretty tough. 

Lots of steep stairs & hills to climb but some breaks of a flatter surface throughout. Beautiful views of the ponds & cliffs along the way. Then stairs, stairs & more stairs 

Finally we made it to the top!  Views were gorgeous and it was worth the challenge! 

If we could have changed anything, we would’ve brought bikes as it would’ve saved us probably an hour or so there & back. Also, bring lots of water! We crushed at least 3.5L and that was not enough! 

All and all, fun hike and it was worth it!
Beautiful views but lengthy! We didn’t train for the hike other than being consistent with walking, and we completed it in 7hrs. Started just before 8am. Brought lots of water and snacks!
Scenic views. Stunning Lake Superior .
Absolutely amazing trail. It's worth the toll on your body lol the views are spectacular.

Went camping at the park August 2024 
Novice hiker here! It was a killer it took 6-7 hrs 

We biked the 7 km at the bottom of the climb! The ascend was pretty steep and there were lots of stairs. There was a part up on top where there wasn’t any signage so we just followed others and were directed to the top of the giant, which had spectacular views! DONT MISS IT! 

Start earlier in the morning so you don’t get the afternoon sun ☀️ 
take lots of bug spray!
Half covered in snow and the other half is basically a river
DO NOT plan this trail in the spring.
Beautiful as always, windy as heck

Breathtaking views toward the top of the trail - most of the distance is through the forest with a few lookouts onto the lake. On the way back we were wishing we had a bike as those last 7 km walking back on the flat-ish part of the trail were gruelling.
Great views everywhere. You can ride a bike to bottom of the mountain.
The view was amazing !!

If you have bikes, definitely bike the first part - 7 1/2 km and uneventful. Save your legs for the main event! There is a place to lock your bikes (bring lock). Also note top of the trail is a loop and the signage isn’t super clear for that one part (otherwise it’s very straight forward). Don’t miss the gorge! The trail description had me a little nervous about fitness and heights but wasn’t a problem. First part of trail (after the bikes) is STEEP with lots stairs, but easier after that.

This is a really beautiful hike, we arrived at the park just before 8am and we’re one of two people parked. They have a little wifi booth by the toilets in the car park for you to grab a permit if you haven’t got this in advance. 

The trail is well maintained and has beautiful views along the way. Incredibly windy at the top of the giant today so we didn’t stay long at the top. 

We did run into a bear on the trail about 2-3K from the car park on our way back, so be bear aware.
Beautiful hike, make sure to come prepared.
Great trail. Easy running for the first 7 km and then the climbing starts. Outstanding views at the top from various vantage points.
Bike ride to trailhead about 5 miles then hike
A challenging but doable hike! Well worth it for the views, completed in 6hrs 45min without biking the first/last part.

We took bikes which saved us a lot of time. However the trail on a bike is a bit of a climb on the way back.
I have a fear of heights but didn’t have a problem with this hike. At the top I didn’t go near the edge but the majority of the trail is through forest with a couple of scenic viewpoints.i would do it again.

Great trail! Took about 3.5 hours to get up (with lots of little breaks on the steep parts, no bike) and 3.5 down. We did see a bear on the trail and a couple of snakes. The stairs are definitely no joke but the view at the top is well worth it! Make sure to bring lots of water (I drank about 1.5-2L) and lots of food. There are a couple rocky bits that are more difficult and the stairs are a bit awkward/uneven in bits but the trail is very well maintained and well marked.
Best to bike the first trail in as it will save you a significant amount of time. There is a bike rack to lock your bike before the trek up to the trail head.

Amazing views from the top, a few places to stop along the way for breaks/snacks. The gorge lookout was unreal. 
This is a strenuous hike- the distance as well as well as the incline. 
The first 6-7km is relatively flat, then the climbing begins. Uneven stairs, lots of rocky hills and roots to work around. Could have taken more time going up- really pushed ourselves. 
Recommend strong fitness level to complete- it took us 6 hours including the side trail to sea lion lookout and a lunch at the top.
Bike, then hike

The trail is well marked and maintained. The trail to the base of the climb has dangerous shale sections, but is good otherwise. The stairs are appreciated on the trip . It was a good idea to bike the trail to the base, I would recommend it. bring lots of water, wear good shoes, have fun
T
Views are worth the hike, unless it is foggy.
Amazing views
Bike from parking lot to the base of the Top of the Giant Trail then hike the rest of the way ….. very fun trip!
Trail is in good condition, a bit muddy, bring warm layers if it’s a cloudy/rainy day, it’s cold at the top!

SUNDAY, AUGUST 31 - Recently did the Top of the Giant Hike.  I would highly recommend to take a BIKE with you.  Drive up to the SOUTH KABEYUN TRAIL PARKING AREA. Unload your BIKE and go through KABEYUN TRAIL until you reach the intersection with TALUS LAKE TRAIL . Go further along the TALUS LAKE TRAIL until you reach TOP OF THE GIANT TRAIL JUNCTION. Lock your Bikes in BIKE RACK and start the Hike.  About 3.3 km one-way from TOP OF THE GIANT TRAIL JUNCTION to THE GORGE LOOKUT. Basically you can do the first 8 km by Bike and hike the remaining 3.3 km. It took me around 7 hours in total ( including the time spent on THE GORGE LOOKOUT and TEE HARBOUR beach which is about 2 hours in Total) . I saw a bear during the Hike and I would recommend to carry a BEAR SPRAY with you for safety. Hope this helps someone !

Beginning of the trail was alright, but pace yourself, once you're about 7.8km in, you'll be greeted by many stairs (we lost count) taking you up about 216m. The stairs are oddly shaped, uneven and mix of rocks. Bring plenty of water. I'd recommend biking in from the trail head up to the stairs, there are bike racks setup for storing your bike. The lookouts are great after the stairs and on way to the top. Beware there were some bears present when we reached the top, bring bear spray to be safe.

Fairly difficult trail, the first leg of the hike up to the stairs isn't too terrible, just a bit long and some minor elevation changes. It's a bit difficult if you're not used to hooking but doable for most people. The stairs onward however are quite strenuous. You'll need to be prepared, bring enough water and food, and practice on the stair master. There are a lot of steps. Also, there may be black bears at the peak
Scrambles, uphill, roots, we biked in to the base.

Ohh yaah. What an absolutely beautiful hike. We went the beginning of September and the weather was pretty perfect. Cold nights but beautiful mornings and incredible afternoons. I like everybody else says on here the beginning of the trail is beautiful and it is flat. There's a little bit of elevation here and there for about 2 hours. There are a couple of Scenic routes along the way. I recommend heading them before and not after and I'll tell you why. HOOLLLYY #@!*. To be for real. It's not awful. Don't be a b**** I wore toe socks and sandals so I suffered lol. Honestly, depending on your speed the stairs aren't the worst thing in the world. If you're in any kind of shape but going down after you get up there and doing 6 hours of hiking because we did take our time. Was pretty f****** rough. But man it is worth it. Definitely bring trail snacks and a trash bag and don't leave your s*** out there like other people. It's beautiful. It's incredible. It's worth it. Definitely do it and take a rock home as a trophy because you earned it. Hopefully border patrol won't destroy you for that. Anywho, it was a beautiful trail. Take water and have a great time
pretty busy trail! overall not as hard as it is hyped up to be; just long!
Great hike! Bring lots of water, get ready for a grind (the flat part was the worst because it’s so long and boring).
The Gore view is worth the rolled ankles and steep climb. Watch your footing really rocky and tons of roots in the way.

To anyone trying this for the first time.. the stairs are not literal stairs - well in some places it is but it’s a test of mental fortitude and physical fitness of straight up traversing the trail. Actually straight up … 
First 6km you’ll be thinking you’re a monster it’s flat and groomed and beautiful. Then you get to the stairs and you ask yourself how did I get here and why? Is it really that important do I have to see all the pretty views? Yes. Yes you do. It’s majestic. 
Practice ok - by the time the trail ended I was pretty close to just laying on the ground and letting the earth take me because my feet were not used to walking for seven hours and they vehemently went on strike. Wear good shoes over good socks, bring blister covers. 
Went through 2L of water and ran out in the last 2-3km 
Mosquitos weren’t terrible but they existed. 
Have so much fun 
Bring snacks.

A good majority of the hike is very easy, not much incline. however….. when you reach the stairs…. You will question if you’re going to die. that part was very difficult. Once you complete the stairs, the rest of the hike is easy/moderate. It took me 5 1/2 hours. I saw lots of cute garter snakes, tons of pretty birds and some grouse. Drank 2 litres of water. There is wifi at the bathroom by the parking lot and service on the very top of the hike. 
Completed with 34,000 steps, the walk to the actual trailhead is far and you can really feel it on your way back.  this hike is exhausting but SO WORTH IT!!! The view from the gorge is incredible.

I like the part of steep incline up to the top. It’s a little strenuous but not bad (but the wooden stairs were such a pain). The gorge lookout is nice. Good spot for a picnic. Recommend check out Tee harbour and Sea Lion as well.

Done sleeping giant a few times, always a great hike. Pack lots of water and give yourself longer than you might think (6-9 hours in and out) the stairs can be brutal but it’s always worth it for the view! We had a bit of our hike cut out. Took us about an extra 45 mins.
The best and the most challenging trail I’ve ever hiked
I have completed this hike multiple times and it continues to be a good experience.
Incredibly challenging but beautiful. Bring a bike for sure!

Beautiful trail that was definitely worth the climb.  I hiked it with my kids (13 and 7) and it took us 8 hours roundtrip with breaks for snacks and water so it is possible to do the hike with kids without biking it.  I had lots of good snacks, water and electrolyte drinks to keep them motivated.
Awesome, get their early though before large groups do

Good trail. Well maintained but some area is slippery.
Do carry water and food. 
The views are awesome.
Yep I did it, epic, grueling, my favorite view was the top and the parking lot, the pictures tell the story, I’m thankful my body still allows me to do this, if you love hiking this is a must see
Amazing but hard
Very challenging, but worth it.

Challenging hike with amazing views despite the smokey conditions. Bring lots of water (I brought 3 liters and ran out while biking on the return). Good idea to bike the first portion but it can be quite rocky and has some hills. We took our time and took lots of breaks. Start early, wear good shoes, and come prepared. A bit crowded this time of year due to its popularity but we met some great people and everyone was very encouraging. Folks of all ages and skill levels were out enjoying this difficult and rewarding trail.
Wow! Crushed it with our four ROCKSTAR kids (9,7,5 and 3) - Biked to the Talus Junction and hiked the rest! One of the best hikes I’ve ever done!
Beautiful sights at the top - well worth it. Recommended to bike first part if you can, but overall extremely rewarding

I highly recommend you bike the first 7 (ish) km’s, hike to the top of the Giant, and bike back! There are bike racks and trees you can lock bike to.  It was a challenging hike for me and I was happy to get on the bike to pedal back…walking back 7 km’s would not have been fun!
Stairs

Up/down + Sea Lion in 4:45 of hiking time (no bike). Ran some of the way down. Drank 2L of water. First and last 8km are flat and bikeable -- that would have shaved off 90 minutes (bring a lock). Less than 2km of the way up is actually steep, it flattens out at the top as well.

What a wonderful feeling when you finish this hike! Rode an e-bike in the first and last 6km which was a delight! The hike up to the top of the giant and the gorge is a tough go but doable with patience and water! Bugs weren't bad today at all. Stopped in and saw the sea lion on way out which is only 500M extra so why not!

The view on the top was spectacular. One of the best you can get in Ontario. We started the trail at 7am and got back to parking lot  around 2:30am. The flat part could be annoying especially on the way back when you are really tired.
Have bug spray and good amount of water.
Worth the view even though it wasn’t the greatest with the smoky sky.

The Tee Harbour beach stops and views of the gorge were cool, but I would not do this again unless I had a bike for the 7km stretch at the beginning and end of the trail. 14km total of boring, flat, buggy trail.
No phone service till top of the giant. Bring alot of water. Rode my bike the 1st 5 miles, rest hike.
The flat part is a bit of a slog at times. Quite a few people used bikes and that’d cut off 60-90 min I’d guess
Got rained on, still had a blast.
Very weather dependent for the views. Way too much fog to see anything once you get to any of the viewpoints today, but it's nice to be in the clouds

Easy trail to start with but hard at the last 3 kms. If you're from BC, it should kinda feel like the Swatamus Chief at the end, or if you're from Quebec, Le Secotora from Jacques Cartier National Park. In short the last push is a steep climb. No poles are required but recommended for the descent down. Please bring lots of big spray. Tons of mosquitoes out there, but luckily the hike is mostly shaded so we didn't run with sun screen today. Just bug spray.

Having a bike with significantly cut down on the longest part of the trail (especially on the way back because it feels so gruesome). Bring lots of water and wear boots. There is no scrambling, but lots of stairs, rocks, and roots. Stunning view.

Finally did this bucket list hike! First 7.5km are flat and a little boring TBH. But the views at the top are amazing! Took me 5.5hrs with all stops (including a half hour break at the top) - I did run about 4km of the flat part k the way out though.

This is one if our top ten trails for the year! Amazing views, uncrowded, beautiful forests. It was a bit of a slog to get out to the climb, and a little muddy after all the rain, but so totally worth it when you get to the top!
The best hike that I’m never doing again.
Challenging hike. After 6km there is elevation.

We did this trail yesterday, July 9, and it was a great trail but definitely difficult. Make sure you bring more water than you think you will need, especially if you are walking the beginning part rather than biking. The first 8 or so km is pretty flat with a few very minor hills. You are mostly in the woods so it’s pretty cool but the top is pretty warm. Bring a lot of bug spray as the bugs were really bad, especially the flies at the top. Once you hit the break off point to go towards the giant it gets very steep very fast. The incline is a mix of stairs as well as spots of just dirt and rocks. There are a several flights of stairs. Be careful on the stairs as the steps are oddly spaced. I am 5’2 and I struggled to get up some of them as well as back down them. The trail on AllTrails seems to be closed for this season however there are also very few trail markers so we just followed where it had looked like people had gone before we still needed up at the top. Once you get to the top there are a few lookouts but keep going to get the gorge. We ran into some people on the trail about a dozen but for most of the trail we were alone. It took us about 7ish hours with us stopping for a hour at the top and a few   Places along the way.
The length of the trail is the real challenge. The trail itself isn’t technically difficult. Make sure you bring enough water. Bug spray!

This is made up of a few trials in one. We went early July and the only thing that made this trail really suck was the mosquitos and flies. We were swarmed the ENTIRE hike... so bring bug spray or cover up! 

Parking lot --> Sea Lion trailhead (0.7km)
Hike the Kabeyun Trail (6km)  - flat, quite boring, which made it feel much longer 
Along the coast (1.5km)
Steep incline up (0.8km) - this was quite rough, prob fewest mosquitos 
Top of the Giant Trail (2.1km) - first km was challenging, then the last km was a breeze

I did this hike on May 22 and conditions were great! We started early and it wasn’t too hot out, so was perfect. This is a LONG hike so be prepared and have lots of water and snacks with you. The views at the top are worth it!

Very beautiful hike. Easy to follow, very well marked. Beautiful lake views & Beautiful canyon views. I would say it is moderate hike but just because it is one of the longer ones, the walk is pretty easy.

Incredible trail. I found it difficult with all the stairs but just paced myself. My golden enjoyed it too, no other views like this in Ontario, except maybe The Crack. Phenomenal experience, the walking in and out did add a longer timeframe, bikes a great option if you want to save time.

From reading the reviews I was expecting an incredibly challenging hike but it wasn't! It's long, so account for that with water and food but the actual ascent is nowhere near as bad as I expected (and it only took us 5 hours including a stop for lunch). If you're reasonably fit and have done any hikes in the rockies then this will be easy peasy for you. Myself and my 2 chihuahua mixes loved it. The views were fab at the top.

Half of the hike is just a dirt road which is kinda lame. Definitely bring a bike if you have one. There are racks right before the actual elevation gain starts. After that it’s great. Challenging steep ascent with absolutely amazing views
4pm is a late start unless

Give yourself lots of time! It's a 6-8 hr hike. 3km of it is straight uphill basically, but the views are so worth it! There's lots of stairs, but once you get past the stairs it kind of levels out again once you're up top. Gorgeous views! Well worth it! Highly recommend!

I though it would be a medium hike but after not hiking for a long while this was pretty hard. I thought the 600m elevation gain was a bit off but actually it's  pretty accurate, just felt harder since I havent done  any hard long trails lately. There are a ton of wooden stairs on the climb up, would be hard coming down if you have knee problems but  poles would help a lot. The conditions were perfect, cool and a little windy at spots. The bugs are already getting bad but the view was worth it. The fog lifted so you could  see the cliffs but the islands  in the lake were very faint. Maybe haze from the fires or just from the rainy days, not  sure. We walked the entire trail,  saw around 15 people, half of them biked to where the hike up starts. There is a bike lock up area. Well worth it, bring water and some good snacks for the view.
Amazing trail but difficult hike! Take it slow on the last 3 km with small steps and you can do it! Pit toilets are available throughout the entire trail.
Carry a decent amount of food and fluids. If not biking until the steep part, you can expect a long trail.
Challenging,lots of steps

A bucket list hike for anyone from Ontario. The first/final 7km of the out n back are quite dull, which for a hike this distance is pretty significant to me so I’d consider taking a mountain bike for that segment next time–there are bike racks where you can lock up when things start to get interesting on foot. Really nice views of Superior and the gorge at the top.
gorgeous and clean

Great trail if your knees can handle it! Very steep slags.  Hiking poles recommended as well as waterproof hikers for this time of year. Trail was flooded in small manageable sections. Lots of mud.  Many partridge, squirrels,  some deer, a raven, and an overly optimistic chippy who's clearly been fed by people.   Great thunder boxes en route.  Would recommend downloading for offline use as there is ZERO cell service, which is perfect.  Bring lunch and enjoy the view!
Great day for it. Still some water on the lower track but fine biking through. A few trees down up the top which made it easy to walk off track.
Very muddy and icy at some parts. A part of the trail is underwater so you have to take another path. The view was breathtaking
Did this in later December. The snow makes things more tricky but not impossible. Trail is very easy to see
Please take care of yourself!

Not very difficult to find the entrance to the Chimney. Rock garden starts almost 5 minutes after the turnoff. Very fun and memorable climb. Takes about 40 minutes from bottom to top of chimney hike. Wouldn’t recommend on a wet day.
Multiple good view points after the main incline
Stunning view, there are view points on the way.  The view is worth the long hike.
Give yourself time, maybe hbijevthe 16 km main trail to expedite the time spent

This was probably my hardest hike to date. The elevation with the rocky path and oddly spaced stairs make it difficult both going up and going down. If I didn’t have a wonky knee, I’m sure it would have been easier. Poles are very helpful! We were told to allow for 12 hours but completed it in 8. The views are amazing! It was crazy windy the day we went so it wasn’t busy.

This was a bucket list trail. Although the views and sense of accomplishment were high. I don’t see myself doing it again. The first 5.8km are long well groomed path (bikes would be ideal you can lock them before you start ascending)  when you start going up it doesn’t stop and its tough poles saved me the steep climbs are not forgiving. Give yourself 6-8 hours. There are not of areas so stop and rest. Bring plenty of water. The wind was insane when I was there but was able to see and enjoy the views. By the end my legs, feet and pretty much everything else was drained and done. Pretty sure I cried tears of joy when I seen the truck.
Really long trail with an almost vertical climb towards the end.
S

About 15 miles of walking from the parking lot to the top. Last few miles is a climb. Find some sticks to help you up. Worth it but be ready. Don't overpack water,  We did due to all the warnings. Fair amount of snacks, gatorlite, and water.
Delicious views. Saw a porcupine
Bring your A game, if you are not using the bike.. Happy to have completed this epic hike

Beautiful hike. Foggy when we got to the top until 2pm but then cleared up and we got to enjoy stunning views. 
Detour to Sea Lion rock formation on the way out well worth as well.
Highly recommend.

As with some reviews, we took the mountain bikes. The Parking lot Kabeyum trail to the Talus Lake junction took 34 min on bike.  This section is road way wide with packed mud and rocky sections. You may have to walk the bike in some sections (rocks and steeper inclines) well worth biking if you can. At the junction there is a bike rack to park the bikes, we locked our bikes as did all others.  The section from the Talus  junction to the top of the Giant varies 70% moderate 30% hard. The hard section has the big elevation change, but there are stairs to help out the most difficult parts. This section took 1 hour 34 min to the top with a couple of short breaks along the way.   It was the start of fall season when we went and no bugs at all. We started the day in the fog but the upper elevations we were above it.
Easy approach walk, followed by a stiff climb. The view is worth the work, and the top has lots of good rocks to sit on.

24k of ankle breaking walking with some sketchy switch backs only for the view at the top to be completely foggy with zero view. Even though there are hordes of mosquitoes in the summer, hiking this trail in the fall was not it. Also I got Achilles tendonitis from this as a seasoned hiker

Good long hike with extreme elevations!  Challenging but worth the effort to experience the amazing views! 
Highly recommended!!!
Honestly it was perfect as hikes can be. A lot of the same until you get to the magnificent views.
Best hike
Bring hiking poles and good shoes. Also very windy at the top when we went. Significant increase in elevation too

Completed end of august 27th . Conditions were amazing ! super flat 6km walk from parking lot to the start of incline. Many people bring their gravel bike for that part. There are some wooden stairs during the incline. Also watch out for loose rock. Lots of beautiful view points along the way. Deff worth the hike! Took 4.5 hours round trip.

long trail with some steep elevation gains, but there’s stairs for portions of the hike and the view at the top is GORGEOUS.  also saw a couple guys unicycling on the trail so it’s totally doable. highly recommend!

Enjoyed this hike for the second time. This time I walked the entire way instead of biking the beginning and end just so I could get some training miles in. Still one of my very favorite hikes. Trail in great condition, not very busy and incredible sounds, views and peacefulness.

As an experienced hiker I wouldn't say this trail is hard it's just very long, the 14km out and back of flat terrain is smooth sailing, I did this trail yesterday on the hottest most humid day possible which made it more of a challenge but I must say the views at the top of the gorge are totally worth it, I did this with the sea lion in roughly 6 hours (not including the time I spent at the top)

Much easier trail than expected. My girlfriend, dog and myself did this trail right after we did talus lake trail (which to my fault was not properly prepared for) and we were shocked at all the wooden steps and easier step placements. The beginning and end of this trail is mindnumbingly boring but luckily we only did it one way back. (Started from Marie Lake louise campsite). 

I'd say it's moderate difficulty at best, my Gf did it in crocs after 4 hrs of previous hiking at 5'-2".

Bring lots of water and snacks especially if you bring a dog to the top. Less creeks available. 

We went in late August and not many bugs at all so that's a big plus. Nice views and pretty rewarding if you take extra time apart from the 6 hrs alotted to actually enjoy it. We didn't get that opportunity because we ended the day at 11hrs and 40km hiked and I couldn't recommend that less haha.
-1 stars because the first 7km are boring as hell. Rest of the trail is well maintained I did it in my tevas
Amazing trail!!!! Not an easy one but worthed
Well maintained and easy to follow. A couple of technical sections but mostly a moderately difficult one. The long climb will take if out of you.

This hike is HARD and LONG. I’ve done The Crack, Cup and Saucer…etc with no issue.  This one kicked my ass. Bring a bike and helmet, but not just any bike.  Must be a proper mountain bike with suspension. My bike had zero suspension, and I felt my brain rattling over the rocks. . The ride is hilly, rocky, and some roots. Not super easy, but Still better than walking the 8km in and 8km back out. 

Make sure you gave proper hiking shoes/boots. I had my closed toe Keens, but they weren’t good enough. 

Plenty water. More than you think. 

Bring food. 

No shade at the top to enjoy your lunch.

Honestly, I have some beef with this trail LOL let me tell you why. It’s comprised of 3 sections of 3 different trails: the Kabeyun trail to Talus Lake trail to Top of the Gaint trail. When planning our trip to SGPP and trying to research the Km distance of the Kabeyun stretch vs. Talus + Top of the Giant stretch, not only did every online source state a different distance but so did every park-issued map!!! Like I’m talking even two different maps posted right beside each other at the trailhead, one that said Talus + Top of the Giant was 3.5km and the other 4.2km. Well, that section ended up being closer to 6km ONE WAY according to both my Apple Watch and AllTrails navigation. Might not sound like much of a discrepancy, but on a 20+Km trail, every extra Km counts lol. Because we had our dog with us and weren’t sure he could do the whole trail in one day, we preemptively decided to spread the distance of this trail across two days and camp at Lehtinen’s Bay just passed the Kabeyun + Talus junction. Our plan was to complete the Kabeyun section on day 1, then the Talus + Top of the Giant return and Kabeyun back out on day 2. We are experienced hikers and still knew that day 2’s km’s would take us a good chunk of time, even with shaving off the first bit the day prior. And that was before discovering it would be even longer than expected. In my humble opinion, the discrepancies in park-issued maps are a major safety concern and borderline negligent of the park. A trail of this magnitude, length, and popularity demands accuracy in its depiction on maps for safety’s sake, especially when it attracts people from all over of all experience levels. 

So maybe my beef is more with SGPP than the trail itself, because soapbox aside, this trail is pretty spectacular. For those looking for the accurate distances like I was, the Kabeyun section is 7km one way and  the Talus + Top of the Giant is about 5.5km one way. The entire trail was 25km total (not including the extra km that hiking to and from our campsite added). We did not stray from the trail, made no wrong turns, and did not do the Sea lion side trail. 

The Kabeyun section is a breeze. Talus was pretty easy too. The steep sections of Top of the Giant arguably rival the Canadian Rockies in their difficulty, but they are followed by a stretch of flat terrain to let you catch your breath before losing it again the next incline lol. The thrill of reaching the top after such a grind is the best high you’ll ever experience. Start early in the day so you have the viewpoint to yourself and plenty of time to get back down in daylight. Pack out what you pack in and leave no trace. Picked up beer cans left by others. Com’on people. 

We saw no wildlife on the trail, but two others reported seeing two black bear cubs and another said he spotted a wolf on the Kabeyun section. We always carry bear spray to be safe. There is no cell service in the park aside from at the beach and at the very top of the giant. 

If you are inclined to backcountry camp off this trail like we did, Lehtinen’s Bay is the place to do it. Nestled in a bay at the base of the giant’s cliff towering over you, it’s the most beautiful campsite you’ll ever stay at. A bear locker to store your food and bathroom (aka thunder box) are also available at this campsite.

I hiked the Top of the Giant Trail on July 20, 2023 as a day hike via the Kabeyun and Talus Lake Trails. This is one of the most amazing hikes I’ve ever done and had been on my list for awhile. 

The trail starts off along a long, mostly flat section through the forest for about 8 km. You can take a quick detour to the Sea Lion rock formation and also a detour at the Tee Harbour backcountry campsites. There are some pretty views there and it’s the only place that has water access to filter water on the hike. I got through the flat section pretty quickly and moved at a steady pace, reaching the campsites (6 km in) after around 1 hour, 45 minutes. 

The trail then branches off on the Talus Lake Trail which remains fairly flat but starts to gain some elevation with a set of wooden steps. Once you reach the junction for the Top of the Giant, it’s another 3.3 km to the top and this is where the trail becomes more challenging. It starts off fairly flat and passes a beautiful meadow with mountain views, which are the first views along the hike. Then, the elevation begins with steep switchbacks and lots of wooden stairs. The challenging section lasts for around 2 km and the trail gains a lot of elevation in a short time. It was tough and I stopped many times to catch my breath. Once you reach the sign saying “Top of the Giant, 2.1 km,” you’ve completed the toughest part and the remainder of the trail is a mix of gentle elevation gain and flat sections through forest. The trail opens up to stunning views of the Tee Harbour on this section and the surrounding rocky cliffs. Most of the trail is shaded and cool but in this last section, there are more exposed areas to the sun as you are on top of the cliffs. 

Then, you reach the Top of the Giant gorge lookout! There are various side trails that lead to different perspectives of the gorge. The scenery and views were absolutely breathtaking! Don’t get too close to the edge as it is a sheer vertical cliff! I spent around 45 minutes enjoying the views here and eating lunch on a rock. 

The hike back requires steep downhill sections where hiking poles are helpful for extra stability. The flat forested section at the end (especially the last few kilometres), felt super long and monotonous and never-ending. To top it off, the last half a kilometre of the trail to the trailhead is slightly uphill which felt more intense after such a long hike. 

The entire trail (including stops to catch my breath, take photos and lunch) took 8.25 hours. My average pace was 18.5 minutes per kilometre despite being quite slow on the uphill sections and stopping often. This was by far, the longest day hike I’ve done but I still felt pretty good physically and mentally after I finished. 

Things to know: You need a day use permit to access the park and trails (can be purchased in advance for $15.50) unless you’re camping. There is an outhouse at the trailhead, outhouses at the Tee Harbour campsites and a pit toilet along the way. There is zero cell service in the entire park except at the Top of the Giant gorge lookout where you get full bars. Bring lots of water and make sure to filter some water at Tee Harbour so you have enough. Don’t underestimate the long flat section on the hike back - this was almost the toughest part of the trail because you’re tired and sore at this point and just want to sit down. The mosquitoes weren’t too terrible - they were definitely out but with bug repellent and bug repellent clothing, I didn’t get any bites and they didn’t bother me as long as I was moving. Even when I stopped for a second, they were manageable. And as you gain elevation, there are less mosquitoes. They’re mostly in the forested sections. 

This was such an incredible hike. I had doubts before I began as to whether I could do it, physically. But I proved to myself that I capable.

Awesome views! The gorge was spectacular! Thank you for the steps,  they made the climb so much easier
Really nice day hike. Cold rainy and foggy when i went, still amazing

The climb to the top was not bad as the park has invested in building steps! What makes this trail really hard is the length. You'll need an early start to take it at a leisurely pace if walking the entire way. Trekking poles and hiking shoes are necessary. If you can mountain bike, that's a huge win as the last 2km back was never ending.

We hiked this trail September 12th. The main trail is down a wide path along the lake for the first few kms. The side trail to the Sea Lion Lookout had fun terrain but had many confusing side branches. We had the downloaded map so had no problem but had to assist another group of hikers. The Sea Lion was pretty and the water around it was a lovely blue. 

We also really enjoyed the Tee Harbour side trip. We hopped the large rocks and pools for a while to get some great views of Lake Superior. A float plane took off while we were on the rocks and waved at us with his wings. We really appreciated that!￼

Once we started the Talus Lake part of the trail the terrain became fun. It was a great workout going up to the Giant. There were a couple of guys working on stairs for some of the steep sections of the trail. What they had built was very helpful and easier to come down then the slopes would have been. Much appreciated!

There were many outstanding views from the cliffs. The views from the gorge were truly unbelievable! There were several vantage points to take pictures. The sheer height of the cliff faces were unreal. It was the perfect place to have a picnic. The hikers on the day we went up were so nice letting everyone get the pictures they wanted without anyone taking overly long. It was a nice experience. And I must say that the view is right up there as one of the best views I have had the pleasure to experience!

The first part of this trail is fairly flat so the distance isn’t quite as daunting- but the last half is tough. The new stairs are helpful but slippery after a rain. The trail is rocky and covered in roots- wear good shoes! The bottoms of my feet were very sore afterwards. The view is totally worth the hike!

Definitely doable but just long and feet will be tired ! If you have the motivation you can do it. It took us 9 hours and made lots of stops. Recommend lots of bug repellent and after bite.

The view is AMAZING. So worth it.

Honestly the most parts of the trail are uninteresting but the last par and the top of the giant offers an amazing view.

Conquering the Giant

Two years ago, we attempted to reach the top of the sleeping giant.
We had no idea how difficult it was until we failed two times. We learned from our failures and came back prepared to reach the summit.

On Friday, July 22nd, at 9:56 am, we started our journey to the top of the Giant.

Side note, the Sleeping Giant, is an igneous rock mountain in the Sibley peninsula.

One Ojibway legend identifies the giant as Nanabijou, who was turned to stone when the secret location of a rich silver mine now known as Silver Islet was disclosed to white men.

Anyways, back to our adventure, the first phase of the trip consisted in taking the Kabeyun trail using our old mountain bicycles, with a chair attached to my wife's bike and a chariot attached to my bike where my poor son was strapped too .

We biked some uphill and intense downhills, but we made it to a lovely beach alongside Lake Superior. We took a break, drank some Kangen water to replenish our energy, and continued until we could not go any further as the bike trail ended.

The second phase started where we left our bikes, and we all started the hike using the Talus trail. There were some challenging parts, but my kids champed it out and continued until the junction of Talus. From there, we hike alongside Thunder mountain through a beautiful forest covered with many different ferns.
The hike was gorgeous, but we had to keep a steady pace because we knew it would take us a long time to reach the top.
We stopped at a lovely big tree and had some lunch to recover energy until
we reached the bottom of the giant.

Phase three started with the ascension
of what they called the Stairs. In our previous attempts, we did not reach the stairs, so we had no idea why they called it the stair. Let me tell you, as we climbed up, the path became narrow and, at some points, risky. We had to be extra cautious with our kids, but they were having a blast. My son was climbing like nothing, and at some points, we had to ask him to slow down .

The stairs were the most challenging part of the whole trail and took most of my energy and our water. 

Once we reached the top,  we were greeted by other hikers and clapped my kids for making it to the top. We thought we were done, but to our surprise, we had 30 more minutes to reach the end of the hike to the gorge.

We took pictures, rested, and kept on going.  Our kids were so impressed and did it all by themselves. We did not carry them even though we asked them, but they wanted to do it themselves.

Phase four, that was the last part; it felt like it took forever because we ran out of water, and we were depleted. Finally at 15:41, we reached the trail's end and completed the top of the giant.

Well.....we reached the top of the giant, we took pictures had dinner, but NOW we had to head back before sunset lol

We were exhausted, but we knew we had to return the same way. The downhill was more accessible on the legs but painfully on the toes as you constantly put all your weight on them when climbing down.

The way back was not as fun as before; with the help of some friendly hikers who shared some of their water, we made it down the stairs, back to Talus, and back to the bikes. The bikes were excellent for the kids as they finally had a break. They fell asleep while we biked back.

We finally made it to our car at 19:57, and we were sooooo happy to see our SUV.

This was the most arduous hike we have ever done, and we will never forget it.
It was not easy for us, and our kids impressed us. We will never forget this beautiful moment we all shared and we will be back next year for the last challenge.

Beautiful but challenging trail.  Didn’t see many other hikers and had lots of time to enjoy the lookout on top!
Trail is good. Little buggy at the beginning of the day. Forgot to turn the app on until I was 5km in. Total distance was 22.6km. It’s a challenge but worth the views. Would do again.
Amazing views well worth the difficult hike.  Bring lots of water.
Epic view. Very easy hike.
Sooo difficult ! But soo beautiful

So there are really two parts to this hike. Parking lot to Tee Harbour (Kabeyun) to the bottom of the ascent is a pleasant walk. Long but not hard. It’s worth the time to enjoy Tee Harbour and explore a bit. There’s also a privy in Tee Harbour. 
Now, the ascent to the Top of the Giant is a different beast. There are stairs. Lots of stairs. High stairs. And they seem to go on forever and ever. However they do end. And then you have to keep going, but it’s not so bad (but you are still going up). 
And then you make it to the top, which is totally worth it. You need to spend some time exploring the top. Go to all the sides to get the different views. Make sure to take the gorge path out to the Thunder Bay side. Bring a snack and relax. 
Then you get to undo everything you just did.  It’s not so bad. Stop and take a swim in Tee Harbour on your return. Then settle in for a long walk back to the parking lot. 
We spent about 8 hours on the trail but about 2 hours were spent enjoy the different sights and stops. 
Worth the time and effort!

Very buggy this time of year. Took about 8 hours total. Bring 3-4L of water on hot days or have a way to get more water if you can!

Choose early Spring or much of Fall unless you want to donate a lot of blood. Mosquitoes galore!! Absolutely brutal!!! Notice my exclamation points. 

The “Giant” is filled with fascinating geological landscapes. Lake Superior: all US states that border it (Michigan, Minnesota and Wisconsin) and of course Canada (Ontario) remains criminally overlooked in the world of hiking. 

The Ontario section of Superior contains the longest shoreline compared to the US States, Michigan is close. Also,the Ontario shoreline, I believe, has the most wow factor on a map, and even when you see it in person. But much of the Ontario shoreline is not ideally addressed for hiking enthusiasts. The season is perhaps too short to truly enjoy it without serious preparation and work.

My phone ran out of power for the last 2.5 miles. It’s approximately, as
advertised, 14 to 14.2 miles out and back.  We stopped a lot, but you can do a round trip with a 45-60 minute lunch at near the top, Gorge Lookout, in about 6 to 6.5 hours.). Bear in mind the Gorge Lookout is not the highest point of Sleeping Giant, go NE to reach this point, which is a little over 1800 feet
or roughly 1200 feet above Superior.

Great hike. Trail well maintained.

I am not in the best of shape, however I did complete the trail. Well worth the effort. Really enjoyed seeing my old stomping grounds again after 40 years. Don't forget to pay the daypass fee at the camp store before you get to the trailhead.

Iconic views

Completed June 19, 2022 during a thunderstorm and it was an absolute downpour. The path towards the base of the giant is very long and became a stream. Everyone in our group was wearing waterproof shoes, jackets, rain pants and we all soaked through. The incline isn't very long and not hard at all (even with it being slick from the rain). There are some high steps you'll need to take but not too many. We waited out the storm prior to reaching the Top of the Giant to avoid getting struck by lightning. Made it to the gorge and back in 6h30m with about an hour of stops to let the rain subside. Would definitely recommend doing this hike, the view from the Top of the Giant and the Gorge Lookout were absolutely STUNNING. Maybe just don't do it when there's a thunderstorm. The challenge is the distance, 23km is a lot of steps and we were all pretty fatigued walking the flat 9km back to the car. There is a bike rack at the bottom of the incline so you can bike in to avoid the grueling 2hrs of flat.

“Moderately challenging” is a fucking joke. This is extremely challenging and literally made me question my will to live. I went may 4 and there was still snow on the ground. Kept getting stuck due to the steep snow and there was no proper trail markings to ensure we were on the right path. We got to one point where the snow was so deep we were stepping in frozen lake under it. We were 7 hours in and were lost and were no where close to the top so we turned back due to a bear print. It’s been a month and I’m still in pain due to the hike. If you want to even attempt this go during the hottest months of the year. Cause this was literal hell
slow but challenging. a few bugs and mud spots but easy to manage with the proper attire.
Absolutely gorgeous when we did this in September of 2021. Go early, wear some good shoes, and prepare for wind!

Awesome is all I can say. And a great day with no bugs
Excellent weather day. Trail has now just a few short muddy spots but very passable. Stunning views from the top ridge- worth the long hike!
Very nice hike, worth the views, but you will need more time, at this time a bit muddy
Challenging.

Long hike but the views are worth it

Honestly, even with the right gear, the top of the giant trail is hardly doable at this time of year. 2 feet of thawing snow had me sinking waist deep with every step so I decided to turn around and not do the top of the giant. The rest of the hike was great though! Sea Lion was lovely as well.

This was a gorgeous trail and the views at the top of the giant was astounding! Very beautiful but be aware if you so have a fear of heights/vertigo. 

We did the trail a couple days ago (end of April 2022) and it was incredibly difficult due to the snow. We started in the morning when it was chilly and the 3-4ft snow was hard enough to walk on top, but on our way back it felt endless since the sun melted the snow a bit and our feet kept falling into the snow. We were essentially trudging through 3ft of snow on the way back. Snow shoes may not have helped because there were already so many holes created by other hikers - thus reducing the amount of surface area to distribute your weight with snowshoes. However, we wore micro spikes which were essential for traction on slippery snow or ice. Later in the day on the way back we also walked through 3km of ankle or knee-deep ice water since the snow was all melting. We did have the proper equipment, but it was extremely tiring because of all the snow (which also buried all the stairs underneath) during the ascent/descent. 

If we did this in the summer or late summer, it would have definitely been a lot easier. I can guarantee that it would have taken us ~6hrs no problem. 

I’m not sharing this to discredit the hike in any way, but just to give a heads up for those who are keen enough to try this in snow. Nonetheless, the view was sure breathtaking!

Highly recommended hiking The Giant! Definitely worth the 18hr drive it took us to get there. Make sure you're well prepared before heading out. Limited cell service of you get into trouble, until you're at the top of the Giant.

Breath-taking views!

Took us just over 6hrs.
Loved this hike!! Definitely worth the 20 hour drive haha
The best! Make sure to leave early so you’re not hiking down in the dark!

The walk in was easy going in hard to walk back after the climb up and down. absolutely gorgeous views. I can't say enough. super challenging and felt so accomplished after this one. My first super long hike and it was definitely a great choice!
Great hike!
Great trail. Some wet spots. Windy and chilly summit
long trail, beautiful views.
As always, it's an amazing bike/hike to the Top of the Giant. One of my favourite trails in the area.

If you have a bike (preferably a mountain bike), I recommend you bike the first few KMs in as it will save you plenty of time. It’s pretty much a straight gravel path with a few gradual ups and downs and rocky bumps here and there. At the base of the giant, there will be a bike rack and this is where you will have to leave and lock in your bike(s) because the actual uphill hiking portion begins.

The trail itself is not too difficult apart from a short stairs portion near the end where it gets pretty darn steep. Plenty of little viewpoints up at the top though where you can catch your breath and enjoy the view.

Overall I’d say the length of the hike was the most challenging part for me probably because this was the longest day hike I’ve done to date. So you of course should start early because it will be a LONG day. Still, it is definitely doable and very rewarding.

If you’re unsure about whether to attempt this trail, DO IT! If you start and it is too hard, you can always turn around. After reading some of the reviews, we almost cut it out of our trip because we were worried about the difficulty. If you’re in reasonably good health, decent fitness and have some experience hiking, you can do this trail! Was it challenging at some parts? YES! But, totally doable! Start your day early to give yourself a lot of time, take your time and take breaks as you need them! Also, don’t forget to bring water and snacks!

Once you get past this first part, the incline starts gradually and then gets steeper. We were actually surprised at how short the difficult part was. The steeper incline is less than 2 km and then starts to even out. The last bit of the trail to the two lookouts is not overly challenging. The effort is definitely worth it! incredible,  challenging , yet so rewarding , worth stopping at the t harbour trail   took us 10 hours to complete with lots of stops along the way. Def would recommend biking the first part of the trail   we walked it due to not bringing our bikes   .. amazing views   best hike we've done .   

stayed in sleeping giant park so was nice to have a cabin  there to relax afterwards . we were greeted by a mama deer and 2 babies at the cabin. was beautiful end to a spectacular day

We took the advice of others and rode our bikes to the trailhead. It’s a good ride with a few uphills and some tricky areas with larger stones (not too difficult to navigate), but some may choose to walk their bikes through these sections. We enjoyed stops along the way to appreciate the shores of Superior. The climb to the top is steep, but we didn’t find it too difficult as we took our time. We used poles and the ‘rest step’ technique simply because we wanted to save our joints for multiple days of hiking. It was still a long day as we spent a lot of time at the top - bring lunch and a lot of water. The views are spectacular.

My partner and I pushed our one year old daughter in a jogging stroller from the parking lot to the bike racks, then put her in a hiking carrier and we carried her up on our backs. This made it all the more challenging, plus we had a hiking backpack to carry snacks and water. So if you are questioning your ability to hike this trail but you'd really like to and you're not planning on carrying a tiny human on your back, I would say you can absolutely do it. Is it a difficult hike? Yes, absolutely. On the way up to the top, there are sections that are very steep going both up and down and sometimes you have to push yourself to keep going. We had our four year old back at our campsite with his uncle and so we didn't want to take too long, so we only took two short 5 minute breaks on the way up to drink 

and catch our breath. If you can allow yourself time to stop for breaks, it makes all the difference. Would recommend wearing proper hiking boots with ankle support, as I almost rolled my ankle a time or two with the running shoes I wore. Seeing the top was SO rewarding and beautiful. So worth it. If you have an opportunity to do this trail, do it! The hike back to the parking lot zaps whatever energy you have left, so if you have a mountain bike then that's something to consider bringing too. I should note - we did this in September, 2021. This is a great time to do this trail because it isn't as hot by then during the day and there are virtually no bugs. I could not imagine doing it in let's say, July for these two reasons.

Did the entire trail all on foot. Biking for the first couple of KM could be even faster to complete the trail. Stunning view at the top. Bring enough water and bug spray! Performance shoes and comfy clothings are needed.

fantastic but super tough trail, the stairs were killers, never been so happy to see a parking lot like when I did at the end of the trail. it took us 5hr and 45 min with 30 min break all together
