There’s only one spot while hiking up where she felt uncomfortable and got tunnel vision. This hike is not for anyone with bad knees or hips but don’t fear if you’re not a big hiker you can still do this just plan to be there early. It took us 7 hours. When you get to the gorge you have to walk out onto a rock that juts out at the side of the gorge to take pics like I did with your legs hanging down between the two side walls, this can be freaky for sure.

So here's the thing.  You can hike the whole trail if you wanna walk the whole 22km (which some do) but we chose to bike to the racks and then continue on foot and I think it made the day more enjoyable for us:)  The fun part of the hike is the climb!!  I enjoy a challenging/interesting trail so this was right up my alley (maybe not my husband's lol).  There are many places to stop and enjoy the views.  
Final review - fun trail to walk and worth the effort!!
**Side note: We have two small dogs (12 lbs)  who enjoy hiking and the one would have been fine with the hike but the one is a 4 year old who is blind and would have found the trail too much to navigate.
Awesome

This was definitely a hard, long hike! The first 7km or 8km is a flat walk with slight Ricky terrain, nothing too challenging. There were  people on bikes for this part, which was probably the smartest way to do this beginning. There’s bike racks at about the 7km mark, right before the real challenge begins. Be prepared to hike through rock stairs, wood stairs, boulders, and roots, over and over again for about 4-5kms. It is a challenge and people coming back tried to motivate us by telling us, it’s only about 2kms more. It feels like about 6kms. At a point there’s an opening to a beautiful meadow but then the hiker challenge continues. If you ride a bike at the beginning, it’s probably not that bad. The view are stunning! Breathtaking to say the least. There’s a sense of accomplishment when you FINALLY get to the top. We kept thinking we’re almost there, and in fact we weren’t. So hopefully tomorrow we can be more impressed with ourselves. The hike down, when you’re racing against the sun is very hard. We were fortunate enough to get to the 7-8km mark I mentioned earlier before the sun went down. Although we hiked about 3kms in the pure darkness, making a lot of sounds to scare away any wildlife. We encountered a deer, some eyes in the woods, plenty frogs, and some campers. Be smart and start the hike as early as possible. If you haven’t started before noon, and you’re walking the entire way, just move this hike to another day. My feet and body is busted from this hike, so I’ll appreciate my accomplishment in a couple of days. Lol the hike is beautiful at the top, this is one to be  reckoned with. Good luck!!

Amazing trail. We walked the whole way and other reviews are correct - the last 3k is rough. Our feet were on fire and we just wanted to get out. However, the feeling of accomplishment after completing a 22km hike is like no other! The “stair” climb can be tough and definitely you need good hiking boots. 

Oh and bring more water than you think you need!

I'm going to leave a very honest review as reading the previous ones my partner and I had ourselves very worked up. Walking time for us was 6 hours 15 minutes. We spent much more time then that as we enjoyed each Lookout, took it all in, had a picnic lunch and enjoyed each moment fully.
I'm not what most would say is super fit, I have some chub but we do hike often. My opinion, anyone can do this trail who feels there body is able. Take it slow if you need to, the super challenging part wasn't that long. Take breaks on the uphill and make sure to bring enough hydration. 
For 2 of us we had 2 liters of water 2 Gatorade and 2 propel also 2 powder sachet of pedyalite and a 500ml of water as an emergency but didn't use. Our day we went also was not super hot, if it were I'd suggest more water.

Stop at sea lion if you want on the Way up as you will not want to stop on the way back. But I do suggest stopping at tee harbour on the way back and soaking those feet for a few minutes.

The last 4km of the walk back I'd say is the worst, it's flat and easy but for us the energy was down a bit as the sights and sounds are now behind you. So be prepared for that feeling.

If you have a mountain bike do use it as it would help with that long flat walk back, but if you don't don't worry you got this. Take it in, don't rush and enjoy!
the views from the top are spectacular and worth all efforts.
Very nice trail, but difficult last 5km up. Biked from the provincial park to the base, a little over 10 km. Bike rack at bade to lock up bikes. Suggest biking first leg
Awsome trail :)

This trail was awesome. Seems deceptively easy at first, but gets very steep around “the stairs”. After you climb the stairs (about 1.2km) the trail levels out a bit again. Make sure you get an early start as the parking lot fills up fast.

Great hike & bike combo! With the majority of this trail able to be mountain biked, 10 out of the 14 miles, my husband and I were glad we had them. The trail up was steep and eroded in places, but not too tough. Lots of lookouts close to the top. Follow signs for the gorge trail - this isn’t marked as “the top of the giant” but the knees. And to cool off fast, jump in Superior at one of the campsites!

This hike was incredible!!! We took bikes for the first 6.8km and although a bit rockier than I expected, it was worth taking them.  The views along the climb were breathtaking and the trail was beautiful and peaceful.  We went in pouring rain and that added to the adventure.  The climbs were tough at times but when you got to the top, the views were exceptional.   Take food and have a picnic up there.  Highly recommend this hike.

challenging trail but SO worth it. the views from the top of the mountain are breathtaking. 
Quite busy when we went yesterday (Saturday). Had to get a day park pass for $15, but there are signs posted for free access Monday to Thursday. 
I would suggest bringing more water than you think you need, snacks for at the top, and wear good hiking shoes. I wore runners but next time it would be better if I wore something to protect the ankles as well as there are a lot of roots/rocks and climbing involved.

Great trail. As others have mentioned, the first and last 6.7 kms are flat. You don't mind them as much heading there, but on the way back, they do get boring and tough. Not sure why the park is not renting bikes due to the pandemic when other ON parks are renting canoes and kayaks. Anyway the climb is basically from the 7.6 km mark to the 8.8 km mark that ends at what is called the "top is stairs". After this it is mostly a gradual climb to the two viewpoints. What would be helpful on the way back would be a km marker after every km to let people without service know exactly how much they have to go.
Awesome! Amazing accomplishment for our family.

Great trail, better views, no safety nets at the top be careful & sober!! - would recommend mtn bike, we hit the trail from the parking lot at 7 AM, trail & view points were empty!!
-25 minute bike from parking lot to base of trail (roughly 6.5km)
-1 hr 30 min hike from bike rack to the top view (roughly 4.5km)
-45 min - 60 min walk back down to the bike racks
-35 minute bike back (more challenging with dead legs)
- 3 or 4 great view points but keep going until you see huge gorge rock walls! 
- Roughly 4 hrs up and down with some breaks
- Lots of families on trail on our way down and if you take your time - very achievable for the moderately athletic person.

Moderately difficult hike. Most challenging hike I had ever done due to the distance and elevation. Took us about 9.5 hours in total. The first 6 km are flat and easy. Elevation is with stairs and slopes, often unstable footing. Stunning views from the top and totally worth the hike. The map i have here is one way only and we took the same way back. Happy hiking!

Absolutely beautiful views at the top of this trail. This was the most challenging hike I’ve ever done, I did it last year as well and it doesn’t get easier. First 7km is flat ground and then you make your way up. It’s very steep so you’re up pretty quickly. The trek back is brutal and feels like it’ll never end. Nothing about this hike was easy but definitely worth it!

Highly recommend this hike! Yes the first 6 km is old road and could be good to bike if you have but otherwise is fine and the climb up is great hike with lots of views on top- fab all day hike, on hot summer day great to follow with a lake swim!

Long and boring for 85% of the trail. Flat in the woods with no views for 8 km in and 8 km out. Steep hike to get to the top and too much vegetation on most of areas on top. Because of that the main attraction spots end up crowded. Take a bike for the flat parts if you have that option and effort to reward ratio might be better

Hiked to the Top of the Giant with my husband. We are both in our 50s so we a little worried about the intensity. We would have rented bikes at the campsite but because of Covid, there were no rentals. We took the risk without bikes and it was fantastic. Hard yes, and the last km might be the hardest as it is all up hill but worth the effort. I actually thought it would be harder given the reviews so I was pleased that I wasn’t dead at the end. The views at the gorge we’re spectacular. We took 2 litres of water each, mandarin oranges (6) and mini cucumbers as hydration. We did have enough water but we were also conserving  and it wasn’t too hot. Take more water if it’s hot. 
I highly recommend it; just know the last 6 km is long without bikes. (We took 7.5 hours to complete with lots of breaks.)

No wonder it is called Ontario's best day hike. I would recommendend biking the first part as it is quite long. Bring lots of water and food. The smoke was a bit thick but the view was still stunning.

Amazing hike!  I did this with my dog so was not able to bring a bike but sooo wish I could have because that last 6km out is a killer and seems to never end. Bring lots of water!  I ran out by the end.  Two great spots on the trail in (and out) for dogs to have a swim/drink and cool off in the lake.  One half way to the bottom of the trail and one close to the bottom of the trail. Just need a venture a little off course. Start early!  The trail gets pretty busy. I was on the trial by 730am and saw no one for 5km!  Got to enjoy being at the top alone for 20 min before lots of other people arrived. Bring bug spray too!

Challenging but totally worth it. I’ve been getting back into fitness (5’3”, 205lbs) and had my little 19 wk puppy with me, so the trail took me much longer than average - nearly 6 hours to the top. I’d say I’m the anomaly for that time. The first/last 6km can definitely be done on a bike - it has some slight hills with loose stones, so you’ll want to have an appropriate bike. Bugs weren’t too bad, but some bug spray might be helpful. There is a washroom near the Tee Harbour campground (about 5.5km into the hike). There’s also a nice rocky beach and another nice sandy beach near the Tee Harbour campgrounds that make for the perfect place to soak your feet toward the end of your hike.

Excellent day hike. My fiancé and I biked the first 8km (as the terrain is pretty flat, just lots of rocks and some incline) - there’s a bike rack to park your bike before making your climb to the top. Would definitely recommend biking that part if you can as it’s a long and boring walk otherwise and you’ll want all your energy for the climb up and back down. Took us 4.5 hours total hiking and biking (not counting all the time we spent at the top having lunch and taking our time to admire the view). 

Only other tips I’d recommend are to wake up early (so it’s not too hot), bring lots of water and wear hiking shoes. I couldn’t imagine hiking the way down in basic running shoes or anything without proper grip.

Beautiful trail with a stunning climax at the Gorge Lookout. However, the first 8 km is pretty flat and uneventful, so I would recommend bringing a bike. Once at the Talus Lake Junction, you'll find a bike rack. The trail is very easy to follow, however it is not very well marked in terms of signage besides junction points. I met three people on the trail that almost turned back early as they thought they were lost. As long as you are on the Talus Lake Trail, just follow it up the Sleeping Giant and eventually you will get to the top. All in all, the work is totally worth the stunning view at the end.

Beautiful trail, especially the forest in the first Kabeyun section, and the scenery at the end (for me, it was more the gorge and the terrain at the top than the views per se). Having a bike is definitely useful, as the trail in the first 6km is straight and I imagine would be a bit tedious to hike the entire way. This section is rocky and not entirely flat, but bikeable. There is a place to lock up bikes before the ascent to the top. Overall, a great hike definitely providing more challenge in terms of altitude than most other hikes in Ontario!
Great half day trail. No need for a bike, just 2L of water, food and some gumption...
Bring a bike, you won’t regret it!

Despite multiple coats of insect repellent, I did not have even one minute without a swarm of mosquitoes and flies surrounding and stinging me. The trail was super narrow and the first bench you’ll find is at the very top. Is the view spectacular? Yes it is. Is it worth 8 hours of agony from the insects? Not for me. 

I would recommend this trail to anybody looking for a physical challenge, but if you’re doing it purely for the view, there are better trails.

Hiking shoes are an absolute must. Take at least 3-4 litres of liquids per person.

The first 7-8K is relatively flat (muddy/rocky) but the last 3K becomes narrow and virtually all uphill. I wore running shoes for this hike but would recommend investing in hiking boots because of the mud/rocks/roots and general unevenness of the trail. This would have helped on the way down, which was just as challenging after begging fatigued on the way up. This trail will take about 7-8 hours if you stop for nice lunch and to enjoy the views! If you are in shape this trail is challenging but completely do-able.
The longest trail I have finished in Canada
Amazing view at the end. Worth the 22kms. The last 6kms back is brutal if walking. If you’ve got a bike I would recommend biking the first 6kms.

Did this hike June 27th 2021. Was an overcast, rainy day but the visibility was still great and so were the views!! Left the parking lot around 745 and were one of the only ones on the trail. Made it to the top in 2.5 hours with a few breaks. The stairs were not that bad and the hike overall was not nearly as difficult as other reviews made it seem. If you’re in shape this trail should be no problem for you!! Bring lots of bug spray, water and food.

One of the best views you'll see in Ontario, definitely on the moderate/challenging side. The beginning of the hike is a straight ~8km path with not so much to see then the fun starts. Definitely worth biking that part quickly and then take your time enjoying the next part.
It was a GORGEOUS view!! Totally worth it, pretty easy but would’ve rather had a bike for the first half :)

Went yesterday after a week of rain. Lots of the path was flooded and muddy. The bugs were sooo bad too, used some pretty heavy duty deet spray and am still covered in bug bites. This is not a beginner friendly hike, lots of steep stairs and incline. Take your time. We walked in and didn't bike, biking would take some time off,  which may help because when you come down that last 5.6 km is a slow burn. We stopped at the beach on the way back and was beautiful and a nice rest in the sand.

The view from the top is amazing and worth the almost 11kms up. However, it started to storm at the top and the wind was unreal. 

All in all a really beautiful hike. I will do this again and bring waterproof shoes next time. Don't forget your water.
Good trail condition , but tons of mosquitoes in the morning
Trail is clean and dry the whole way.
Easy until the last few km’s uphill. Beautiful and so worth the work.

It’s beautiful. Yes, first time I did it that long. Hike up we took 4 hours. We took our break we sit somewhere we enjoy every view from the mountain. I didn’t want to get tired or faint. I kept myself dehydrated. Got some nuts from suggestions. If anyone go, do not rush just get a bike if you can which is save your energy and your time. There is some difficult path to ride bike but still you can save your energy to bike or walk with your bike up the hill.Climbing down is way easier but harder is walking in a 6.6 km flat road. We were so excited to going to hotel when we started to climbing down. At the very end my husband lost his energy to visit sea lion but I pushed a little bit and we made it. It’s not too hard but after walking that long path, again hiking wasn’t bad I felt. Do not miss sea lion if you finish sleeping giant. It’s not too bad. They made the way pretty secure.

Did this trail on June 1, 2021. Really beautiful trail as it was equally horrible for my lower body. I strongly recommend  bringing a bike for the first part of this trail (because I didn't and I really wish I had one). Carry at least 2L of water and some food. My knees are crying right now as I'm writing this. 

Me and my wife started on 11 am and pretty much finished at 9pm (took a lot of breaks and took our time with the different lookout points, we also stopped by the Sea Lion Rock Formation on the way back.) 

But yeah, bring a bike as other people suggest. It will save you a lot of time but more importantly it will save your legs because the stairs... oh god the stairs... .

Did this for the first time May 27. This was a great trail! We walked 24km (according to my watch) in 3 degree weather which got up to 8 degrees as the day wore on. First 8km or so were very chill - much flatter, definitely bikeable. The rest of the way was long and pretty steep but nothing unbearable. Some mud spots and obstacles.

Wear good shoes, pack a lunch and lots of water, and ladies, take off your rings if you're not used to the altitude!! My hands were pretty swollen by the end  The views at the top were totally worth it. Can't wait to do this one again in warmer weather!
Did this one last year and highly recommend starting as early as you can.  I left the lot at about 8am and it was very busy on my way down.  Only a couple of other groups at the top when I got there.

The trail was well marked! A group of us  walked in on Sunday May 16, 2021 we started at 8am, took us 3.5 hours to get to the top. The most challenging parts were the stairs and those last few kilometers back to the car. We made it back to the parking lot in 2.5 hours. The views were worth the hard work. I can't wait to do it again in the fall. The only thing I would do differently would be to start earlier, like 6:30 or 7 am.

Did this as a run - So i could try to break a record. Anyways May 11 trip to Top of the Giant. Sunny and perfect conditions. First time doing this in a few years. Was amazing. Perfect place for a run  . lots of rabbits and deer around. The views here were amazing nothing beats Lake Superior Just so many great viewpoints . Highly recommend

Completed May 1st, 2021 conditions were amazing, myself however, I wanted to die. The climb to the top is no joke very steep, it took 7 hours total, with a 30 minute break at the top.  Definitely go earlier in the day as I started at 12:15 and didn’t get to my car until 7:23. I wanted to cry, which I did. I wanted to break my leg just so I wouldn’t have to walk back but rather go via helicopter or something rather than walking myself. But instead I endured it and got heat exhaustion.
I could barely bend my legs so nevermind lifting them. I am now laying in bed writing this to tell you that I currently hate my life and have cried multiple times due to pain and exhaustion.

Unbelievably amazing. Put this on your list. Trail conditions are mostly great, couple of icy spots but nothing one can't navigate. Worth every grueling step you take up those stairs. Be prepared! I had snacks and 4L of water. Thanks to Rogers being crap in Other Ontario, I only have half a recording from the top, and in Battery Saver mode (not accurate). But even with the lack of signs, the trail is easy to follow 99 percent of the time. It's a challenge, but if you relish hikes like The Crack and Cup & Saucer, do this!!

Did 28km loop with stops in between  23 Mar.
Took 10 hours with breaks for pictures and filling up water., very icy going up and down the actual top of the giant trail. Bring spikes and poles. Still deep snow at the top but snowshoes aren't needed.
Pack weight of 25 pounds wasn't needed as the snow and rain expected wasn't there, a light load would serve you best.
Be prepared to go, saw a group trying to start the ascent at 6pm when sunset was at 8.

Completed this trail Jan 16, with cloudy weather and approx -5 temperature. Took about 8 hours round trip to complete with an hour break at the top of the giant. The first 6km were flat and easy, with the remaining six having about two major climbs (the staircase is the hardest). Overall, the trail is a test of endurance more so than anything. There are quite a bit of easy parts making it an overall moderate trail. The whole trail is rather icy until you get to the top so I definitely recommend spikes or crampons. Snow shoes aren't necessary as the trail is well used all the way to the top. The only place snow shoes could have been used were the last km on the top, but i kept mine strapped to my back! Definitely worth it and very rewarding :)

Completed this trail Jan 16, with cloudy weather and approx -5 temperature. Took about 8 hours round trip to complete with an hour break at the top of the giant. The first 6km were flat and easy, with the remaining six having about two major climbs (the staircase is the hardest). Overall, the trail is a test of endurance more so than anything. There are quite a bit of easy parts making it an overall moderate trail. The whole trail is rather icy until you get to the top so I definitely recommend spikes or crampons. Snow shoes aren't necessary as the trail is well used all the way to the top. The only place snow shoes could have been used were the last km on the top, but i kept mine strapped to my back! Definitely worth it and very rewarding :)

We did this hike about a month and a half ago. We did the full 22 km hike since most of it is just a scroll with a view of a lake I would recommend that you just do the last 3km to the top! The view was definitely nice kinda busy, but it was much chillier and windier so dress accordingly for that!

Did it today on an overcast cloudy day with snow and didn't think my views would be as good but they were spectacular. This has been on my bucket list for a long time. I was nervous doing it alone because I didn't know if I had enough daylight but I started at 9:30 and did the two lookouts at the top and then came down and did the short jaunt to the sea lions and was at my car by 3:30. 

I found it was difficult to find a trail map on the official parka website but found info from travel bloggers helpful as well as comments here. Trail is well marked and definitely easy to navigate but would've been nice to look at it before going. 

I'd say it's on the milder end of moderate. The incline section isn't so bad and it's fairly short in comparison to the rest of the hike. Worst part was definitely the end cause it seems to take forever. But I had a lovely, lovely day!!!
This trail must be on your bucket list!

Awesome hike!! The first 8km or so is very flat, if you can bike it, I recommend doing that instead. Then it gets very steep for the rest of the way, it was pretty challenging but definitely doable. And the views at the top especially the gorge are worth the effort!! With lots of stops & a lunch break it took us about 8 hours there & back. Just make sure to save some energy for the long way back.
Wow! Definitely make sure you hydrate well. And go on a good day! The stairs are killer

Mostly a flat trail, the steep bit is quite steep but it’s nothing too challenging. Amazing views!! Actually came out as 25k on my watch with going to the two extra viewpoints, so bring snacks and water, or MTB the first 7k

This is not a moderate hike, Infact the Sleeping Giant brochures and maps will advice you that only healthy, physically fit people, should be doing this trail. You're also hiking up some of the tallest cliffs in all of Ontario, it can get steep as the trail going up is not a very long one. Most of this hike is a flat walk, which many will appreciate on the way back. the majority of people bike most of the way, this saves several hours on your hike, and reserves energy. 

Pack a lot of water. I packed lots for myself, but my hiking partner did not, and she ran out very quickly. I gave her some of mine, thankfully we ran into a group of very nice people on the top who were very over supplied. They gave us 10 water bottles and hiked with us down until the main trail. They told us they carry extra water because their friend was air lifted out due to dehydration. So even though I have always made sure to pack a lot of water for myself, I always carry double the amount. 

This is a trail that will not be suitable for someone who isn't willing to go through a challenge. Please be careful and pack necessities. You will need power bars or a good meal to hike up. Eat a large breakfast before, and start your hike early as you can expect to be on this trail for 5-8 hours and can become dizzy very quickly going up. 

 I have seen many people of all ages on this trail.

So worth it! Took us 6 and a half hours including stopping to take pictures for a while at the top. From the parking lot it was 23.24km on my watch and we walked the whole thing. The terrain was difficult and the 6km start and finish felt like forever but made the incline feel pretty short. Beautiful views of the lake though!! Felt like we were in Norway
absolutely loved it. The end is worth all the kms. Bring a lunch and enjoy the view.

The trail is 22.7 km linear route with about 7 kms (total 14 km) pretty beaten down. We walked the whole length but as others have mentioned, many people bike this section but it is not an easy route for biking too if you are not an experienced biker on rough terrains. The actual ascent is not that bad with the infamous stairs section a lit bit challenging. Views from both points i.e. tea harbour lookout as well as gorge lookout are super amazing (I personally liked tea harbour one better, an unpopular opinion albeit). I have pretty bad knees and if I could do it (obviously with support from my husband and awesome friends), anyone can.

Amazing hike. Do it.

It was supposed to rain all day but we got lucky. Some grey skies but we stayed dry. There was a crazy consistent wind storm. Gusts to 75km that made the top feel downright dangerous. We took shelter for lunch and watch a few pines being pulled off their roots. Wish we could've gotten closer to the edge but we had great views and a unique experience. 

Round trip we were 6hr. Don't let the weather stop you as it can change hour to hour.
Great trail.  Relatively easy until you get to the climb that’s where you’ll get your biggest workout.  Every bit of effort is worth the spectacular view

Awesome view
 worth it!!!

I loved this trail so much!!
The Kabeyun Trail is relatively easy. Once you hit Talus it gets tougher and ultimately the Top of the Giant is the toughest part! This clocked in at 28km on the fitbit, we explored the gorge area and Tee Harbour too, so if you want to do the same prepare for a big hike! So absolutely worth it though. Start early, when I was there, the trail got busy by mid afternoon. We saw a lot of people going up when we were going down. Bank on at least 6 hours to complete the hike, more to enjoy the amazing views. Bring bear bells or remember to make a lot of noise! Ran into 5 people who had spotted bears! Another amazing hike that I can't find on here is Nanabosho Lookout/The Chest of the Giant. It was amazing and quieter ... another huge hike though too and in my opinion, more difficult. I've done a ton of hiking and the Talus Trail going up to Nanabosho has one of the most intensely steep hills I've ever hiked.

We completed this trail last week with a group of 7.  We took our bikes thanks to all the reviews recommending it and it was a great experience.    8 kms of biking each way and quite a steep incline at the end of it.  At the end of the bike trail there's a rack to lock your bikes onto, make sure to bring locks.  Took us maybe 45 minutes each way (a very leisurely pace with overweight middle aged men, lol).  After that, it's 2.5 hours to hike to the top.  We went on a cooler day where 1L of water was enough, but I can see how on a hot day it would be a problem.

Amazing but definitely the hardest hike of my life. When they said this hike is not for beginners they were right. It took us 7 hours with breaks and lunch at the top. Although it is very difficult it’s worth it to push through because the view at the top is breathtaking pictures don’t do it justice.
Well worth the effort.
The best hike I've been on in Ontario so far! A mixture of beautiful scenery and challenging terrain especially in the last half to the top of the Gorge.

Awesome trail. Pretty flat and long for most of it with some challenging steep sections to get to the top but many spectacular views. Would also recommend going to tea harbour crossbar to check it out but the top of the giant views were breath taking. Highly recommend. Took us about 8 hours to do it all with some breaks and time to take in the views. (Phone was dying halfway so only half got recorded)
Amazing hike. The longest I've ever been in. Really tiring but worth it at the end. Bring lots of water and snacks. A camera would definitely be recommended here
Highly recommended biking to the start of this trail. We didn't and we regretted it. Beautiful views but definitely the hardest hike I've ever been on. Bring lots of water and a lunch.

this is a great hike, a little hard on 
the feet coming back being 23km, maybe bike in to base of slope, great infinity pool views toward TB.

Super FUN trail. Took bikes out stopping by the Sea Lion on the way to the Stairs. Some muddy puddles and rocky sections. The views of Tee Harbor and Gorge are a whole mood. Stopped by Tee Harbor for a quick dip on the way out!

Recommend biking (saves time) until the South talus lake trail junction. Bring a lock for the bike rack and continue the uphill climb to the top. Quite challenging, but worth the views! The park could improve signage along the way.

the park map isn't great, but the trail is well marked! the views are amazing. the first 7k are often biked but are relatively flat if you are walking them. the last 3k are right uphill, but well worth the climb

Quite flat for the first half or so. Gets steep/hilly after the junction. Whilst going uphill, there are lots of sections in between where the trail goes flat, so it eases out. There are too many reviews suggesting 3L of water. We went with about 1.5L per person and we had enough. 2L would be more than enough (including electrolytes). I personally wouldn't recommend carrying the extra litre of weight. 
Biking the flat areas would make the hike more enjoyable (we just hiked). Check with the park for bike rentals. I did see signs on their information board about kayak and bike rentals. They were closed due to COVID when were there. Athough, these things constantly change.
Once you've topped off, have fun making your way on/around the rocks when you get up there. Enjoy the breathtaking views.  Prepare your knees and joints for the descent
Challenging at times but worth the trek !
Extremely flat and long in the beginning, challenging once you begin ascending. One of the most rewarding hikes, with the views at the top being unbeatable!
Well maintained. Interesting sights. The stairs were a helpful addition. The hike to the top was totally worth the view.
Beautiful trail. It's hard,

My buddy ripped a Juul for 15 hours straight on the drive from Toronto to Thunder Bay, ate a burger and fries for dinner along with two Coronas and three darts the night before and also hit a weed pen. Halfway through the hike his right nut got twisted and busted his knee. We still ended up completing it in under 6 hours. Path was great and signs were easy to follow. Great experience overall.
Incredible hike, worth every meter of elevation to get there. Highly recommend the extended Gorge trail when you get to the top. Proceed with caution!!

Challenging trail but rewarding views at the end. The first 6.7km is dead flat so it’s recommended to bike this portion in order to save some time. There is a bike rack to lock your bike once the ascent begins. It’s doable without bikes but you will start losing your mind on the flat part on the way back after such a long hike. If you are walking the flat part it will likely take close to 2 hours to get to the start of the ascent.

The 4.7km ascent is gradual at the beginning, and then it turns into a staircase which is about a kilometer long. Once you get to the top of the staircase, there is still about 2km of gradual ascent to get to the gorge where the spectacular lookouts over the cliffs are. The entire 4.7km takes about another 2 hours.

All together this hike is 10.9km one way, 21.8km return. Total elevation gain is 250m, not 566m as stated here. You should budget about 4 hours going up and 3.5 hours coming down if walking the entire length of the trail. Bring lots of water and some snacks. Trail is well travelled and lots of signs. Recommend to start as early as possible so you can take a longer break at the top.
Breath taking views. Totally worth it. Did it twice in 10 days. I would go back and do it once more on the fall.

This was tough. 2 hours to the stairs and then another 2 hours to the gorge. It was totally worth it though. 

And on the way back we stopped at the tee harbour beach for a swim in Lake Superior. Wow! What a great way to refresh!! The last 6km was not too hard thanks to the cold swim. 

We spent a total of 12 hours on this trail but it was fantastic!
Great trail. Bring lots of water and some food. Lots of people bike the first bit, but we didn’t. Very steep incline at parts but absolutely worth it for the view at the end.

A friend and I did the Sea Lion and the Giant on foot. Highly suggest biking, as it covers majority of the hike (there are bike racks to lock up). 3L of water was enough to cover my needs, and bring plenty of foods you can snack on as you will need to fuel your body. We walked 27.42kms in just over 8hrs. 

Tips: 
-If you find yourself struggling to get to the top, don’t ask ppl on the way back “How much farther?” as my friend said she could see me start to dread the hike more and more. 
-Prepare yourself to mentally push yourself. It was very rewarding to know I hiked that far for the very first time. 
-Start as early as you can, you may want to stop at lookouts and take a break to enjoy some views.

The view was absolutely breathtaking and worth the 5 hours it took to get to the final view. The climb down was much easier (3hours), but make sure you wear hiking boots. The rocks irritated our feet because we wore running shoes and got blisters. Make sure you bring at least 3 litres of water and lots of snacks. We went on a hot day and ran out of water . Would 100% do this again.
Absolutely amazing, very rewarding views at the end. Bring lots of water, also the last 7kms is tiring after hiking up and down the mountain, recommended to bike or kayak to Tee Harbour
Launched from Silver Islet.  Paddled to Tea Harbour and then hiked to the Top of Sleeping  Giant Trail.  Spectacular views of the harbour and gorge

Great views!
I'm a beginner hiker, and took a lot of breaks, but did it in 5.5hrs and made it through.  Definitely tough!

Great trail with a fantastic view at the end. Like other reviews had mentioned it’s really beneficial to bring bikes or rent them in town to speed up the flat components. We didn’t have a chance to build that into our plans so the extra distance walking wasn’t a big issue on the way out but certainly would’ve been nice to shorten the time spent on the way back. The ascent is tough, but also not as long as I thought it would be. If you slow your pace down to a comfortable climb then it’s doable for the casual hiker. it took us a little over five hours but the pace was quick and it would’ve been nice to slow down more often to take photos and enjoy the view but again the plans didn’t really allow it. Overall would certainly recommend it if you’re in the area and would suggest budgeting 7 hours to enjoy it properly if not taking bikes.

Awesome trail with incredible views from the top of the giant. Left at 7am and were the first there, thankful we did the climb in the morning when it was cooler. You can also bike and cut 15-16k off the walk.

Amazing hike! If you think you’re pretty fit, the hike up the stairs may tell you otherwise!
Gorgeous view the whole way, and the top of the giant is just breathtaking!

3L of water lasted me the whole 7.5 hour trip, as did a ton of snacks. It’s well worth the hustle and make sure to plan appropriately.

It rained for a little bit when I was at the top, so the tree roots on the way down were a bit slippery, but nothing a good walking stick couldn’t help with.

This was a great trail to hike- the kind of hike I’ve always wanted to do. The flat section was easy to navigate even with the muddy sections. The climbing section was challenging but interesting and a great workout and the views when you get to the top...absolutely worth it!! We walked the entire trail in 5 1/2 hours including 1/2 hour at the top for pictures and lunch. Would definitely recommend but good footwear and water are a must!
Great trail. Took 8 hrs on foot. Fairly tough hike for the last 3 km but views and the gorge are well worth the climb. Very enjoyable day but bring a lot of water.

This trail was overall amazing! The views are absolutely stunning over Lake Superior. There is one portion that is called “the staircase” that was on the tougher side, feels like you’ll never reach the top. But once you do the reward is unbelievable. Trail is very clearly marked and there is some historical notes along the marked posts. Highly recommend!!!

As many people recommended, we decided to rent bikes in Thunder Bay and we done the first 8 km on bikes. This is a really nice trail, but both the cycling and the actual hike is difficult. The first 8 km is quite rocky, so if you are new to biking, you should probably just walk. The actual hike is only about 4km to the top from where you leave the bikes (of course, 4 km back too) and it has some steep sections. The view is amazing, so definitely worth the physicial challanges. Bring bug spray. 

As the ride was quite rocky, our GoPro broke down of the bike. Someone found it, and returned it to the park's office. If you are reading this, thank you so much, we really appreciate it.
Such a great and challenging trail, we rode bikes for the first 6km and then hiked the way to the top. Trail is clearly marked and clear.

We did the trail on a sunny and hot day. We rode our bikes all the way from the campground which added quite a lot of effort. One thing to point out is that from the trailhead to the cutoff for the climb, sections are littered with extremely sharp shale. We got a flat tire on our hybrid bike tires: mountain bike tires are definitely recommended, and make sure you have tools and a patch kit (or an extra tube) with you! The trail is steep, but not very technical, it's similar to hikes in Banff...a slog through the forest to get to an amazing view. But what a view once you get to the top. And the crack & cliffs are insane: a truly beautiful spot. The pictures don't do it justice. Definitely in the conversation for top hikes in Ontario if not Canada!

Amazing hike, however if you have just started hiking or not use to hike long distances, bike the first 8 or so km’s. The last 3 km are pretty intense climb but the view is worth the pain. Bring lots of water and food. Try to start the hike early so you can rest for a bit when at the top before coming down. And if you still have som gas left in the tank swing by Sea Lion as well.

Bring a bike if you can. We were travelling across country and didn't have our bikes so we walked the first 8 km. However, once you start the incline, its worth it. The views  from the the top of the giant, specifically the gorge were absolutely amazing and made the 16km round trip of flat boring walking worth it. I also enjoyed the sea lion at the beginning.
Incredible hike - would bike the first half next time
fantastic trail! if you hike it from.the start, be sure to schedule your next day hip surgery! soooooo sore!!

This hike is super stunning! 
Moderate climb near the mid point to the top of the giant for a crazyyyy stunning view across to Thunder Bay and the most massive cliff gorge ever

Very interesting trail. I walked the first 8 km but as everyone has already mentioned, most people just bike there. I uploaded pictures to help others plan their trip. At no point,  I had to climb. Trail is well-maintained and stairs (a lot of stairs) will take you up to gorgeous views. I did see a lot of deers, rabbits and birds. You can make the trail as easy or as difficult as you want. The gorge was magnificent but I felt lightheaded near the cliffs. So I was able to get great pics and enjoy the view but there is no safety rails or anything like this, therefore, be careful! I would recommend starting the hike earlier in the morning to avoid crowds and connect with nature. It is a relatively difficult trail but if I was able to do it, everyone can. Just have plenty of water and don't rush. Enjoy!

Was blessed to hike this on a beautiful July day with no wind or clouds....can't wait to go back again. Absolutely beautiful trail. theres a few km of difficult scrambling up where you gain significant elevation, after that it becomes easy again
Best trail ever! So beautiful!
Make sure to bring a bike for the beginning portion. Beautiful views on the way up.
One of my favorite hikes thus far. There are so many things to see on the way up.
Definitely worth the hike to the top. Amazing views. First section is fairly monotonous and would recommend biking this part (there's bike racks available after this section).
Great trail. Very steep at the top

This was a nice moderate trail that took us just under 7 hours to complete at a leisurely pace, with a few stops. Highly recommend walking the extra 0.9 km to the Gorge once you’ve reached the top. The view is exquisite (just don’t get too close to the edge)! The first 8 km from the parking lot are pretty flat and boring, so if you have the possibility, take your bike (though the trail is quite rocky, fair warning). Took us about the same amount going up to come down and overall was an enjoyable hike (with a few sore feet to remind us of the journey). :)

my dog and i did this one a rainy day hence why it was muddy. we walked the entire distance but highly recommend biking the first 6km, there is a bike lock up before entering the stairs. when you see the red sign saying trail closed due to rocks falling, etc, continue straight through. was a bit confused at that point. awesome view with friendly people throughout trail.
excellent trail. nice view. worth it.

I did this hike with 5 friend. Had one roll their ankle a kilometre in, so he turned back. The trail is very rocky at points so it is best to wear good foot wear. As mentioned the 6km hike in is best done with a mountain bike. We foot slogged it. I highly suggest taking a peak at some of the openings to lake Superior before making your way to the trail head. These are some of the views you will be seeing from the top of the trail so it was nice to take it in from ground level first. Bring lots of water as there is very few areas to pump/filter water. The "climb" section was a good workout, one member of our party was a little slow with it and we waited in case anything happened to them. The views are defiantly worth the hike. The way down is significantly quicker. I'd avoid this trail if rain fall is heavy or has been recently. We hiked it on after a day of scattered rain and it was very manageable, but we could definitely see how navigating in very wet conditions could be hazardous.
Amazing trail and view! Long as hell tho
if you can bike from the parking lot to trail head - do it! Still a manageable hike but that 6k trail in/out is long to finish your day. The gorge is worth it no doubt though!

Rewarding views at the end of this hike. Biked the first portion on Kabeyun Trail, this took just under an hour. Lots of rocks and muddy in some parts, there were a few stretches I had to walk my bike. The hike to the gorge took a little over an hour. The path was well traveled, lots of hikers on a Saturday. Including time spent at the top, 4.5 hours round trip. Brought lots of water and snacks, used a lot of bug spray.
Awesome views from the top! Gets a bit steep at some parts, but overall a great hike!
Great trail if you want to challenge yourself. Trail takes around 7-8 hours to complete, but rewards you with amazing views and photos!!! Would totally recommend.

A great hike for people who can hike great distances and elevation. The hike was about 14 miles round trip and took me 7 hours. Most of the trail is flat. The climb is hard and steep, but well worth it when your get to the top. Trail marking isn’t good. Make sure to bring a map.

I did this trail with my 4 girls ages 9, 11, 13 & 16. We went all the way to the gorge. Was an amazing accomplishment for all. They did really well. The hardest part was the last 6 km out. Every bend we took we hope for the parking lot. It felt so long after 18 km of excitement. It took us 6.5 hours with a short lunch at the gorge and a pit stop to skip rocks  and make inukshuks by the water on our way out. We are all pretty active and resilient so it could take others longer. We were very tiered, sore and thirsty with only one bottle of water each for the trip. Wanted to keep it light since I had a cooler bag lunch packed for all of us. Be ready with water for when you come back and have a really great rewarding dinner planned. Amazing challenging trail! Amazing stay at sleeping giant Marie louise provincial park. Want to go back for the head trail.

Did the hike July 6 2019 it is an extreme hike as the last chunk was steep uphill. But people of all ages, shapes and sizes were on the hike, tough but doable and the "juice is definitely worth the squeeze."

Incredible views from the Top of the Giant. The last couple of kms are pretty much straight up,  steep, tough climb, but absolutely worth it! Bugs aren't too bad, as long as you keep moving. Lots of shade.
Absolutely beautiful! Biking the first 8km helps, lots of bug spray needed from 7-10am, and don't skip out on the gorge - go right to the end, you will not regret it!

Long hike with some steep sections. Did this trail in 2012 over Labor Day weekend. The talus field by the lake was fun to pick your way through. Incredible views of Lake Superior. Definitely was sore after this hike!
Did this trail last fall. Awesome hike. Advantage of fall hike is no bugs. Would recommend this for anyone able to hike inclines. Some section are serious up hills. But worth the work.
A tough 14 miles in the snow... Great hike!
Steep climb, lots of stairs. I’d recommend biking in from the parking lot to the trailhead (5km ish) and then hiking from there! There are bike racks and everything. Nothing beats the views
Lot easier to bike, this bike/hike should take about 4-6 hours biking and 6-8 hours hiking.

This is probably in my top 5 best hikes I’ve ever done. I think the distance probably turns many people away but I promise the views make it worth it. The cliffs up there need to be seen to believe. I saw many pictures before going on the trek but nothing prepares you for the real deal in person. The 1-2 kms is almost straight ascent in my opinion wasn’t bad but I do a lot of hiking and an fairly endured. 
If you’re gonna do the trek, start early. This allows you time to spend up top as well as detour over to Tee Harbour which is gorgeous (you’ll see signs for it along the way) and get back to your vehicle in time the dinner. It took me and my husband 6 hours or so to complete this hike.

the first part of the trail (kabeyun trail) was relatively flat, lots of rocks & mud, we regret not bringing our bikes, it would of made the first part much quicker. we took the extra 1km to the "sea lion rock formation" an easy little hike, worth it. there is a bike rack at the Talus Lake trail where you turn off the Kabeyun trail. the talus trail was nice, some inclines! the 3km up to the Head of the Sleeping Giant trail was a fairly challenging 3km, quite steep. the extra 2km to "the chimney lookout" are so worth it, and youre up there anyways might as well do it! those 2km's are easy. such beautiful panoramic views of Lake Superior, Thunder Bay & the park. we stayed at the top for half an hour. the entire 24km + 1km for the rock formation took us 5:30hours. The views are amazing, no pictures do it justice!

We did a combination mountain biking and hiking. Definitely recommend biking the first part of the trail to the base of the giant. They do have bike racks at the base. The hike up was brutal and quite the workout. The top of the giant was gorgeous and the view made it worth it. One of the hardest hikes I’ve done.

A fairly easy trail, ridiculously easy to follow up to the knees. A gorgeous and very rewarding view make it well worth it. The trail is less easy to follow if you continue around it so keep your eyes open. Watch for wildlife and enjoy the lakes and trees that engulf you.

Pretty challenging hike due to length and steepness once you start the climb from the base of the giant. I recommend biking the first portion between the parking lot start point and the base of the giant trail (there are bike racks). The final view point are unbelievable and totally worth the trek!

one of my favorites at sleeping giant! The way up (last few miles or so) were definitely the most difficult since it was humid. Plus the ascent up the mountain was pretty steep in parts. However it was a great hike and I saw many kids and dogs too. The views were worth it and I'm going to have to go back for a weekend trip.
One of the best hikes you will find for a scenic view.

One of Ontario's most stunning hikes. I enjoyed it once the ascend up the cliff began. There is a lake right before the climb that you may use to filter water. Since this is a long hike, mind the bugs and be prepared.

Stunning! The first portion is a little dull (biking it would certainly cut down on time!), but once you’re past Tee Harbour, things start to get interesting. The top section would likely benefit from more trail markers, but it’s fine. The views are absolutely incredible and well worth the steep climb!
Amazing way to spend the day with a gorgeous lookout at the top. It was also a good trail for my German Shepard. The bugs were not bad this time of year (July).

My family and I traveled from Wisconsin, USA to hike this trail and it did not disappoint. The trail is well marked and easy to follow. The first part of the trail goes down past Seal Point lookout. It is about 3 miles long and is quite flat, but follows the shore line, so you get to hear the lapping of the waves. You reach a couple of check-marks along the way, but make sure to stay to the right and follow the trail signs. 

When you actually reach the Sleeping Giant trail, the climb is pretty steep with roots and rocks and a lot of undergrowth that obscures the trail a bit. When you make it to the very top there is a sign that points you to a 2km trail along the ridge—do it! You’ll come to a few different false lookouts, but continue on and you’ll reach a lookout with a few trails veering off. Take the one going into the forest, follow it for awhile and follow the blue arrows. You’ll come to an absolutely gorgeous lookout over Lake Superior. The ravine is beautiful and you can hear the echoes of the birds. 

It’s a long hike, but the view at the end is totally worth it!

I'm heading up Top of the Giant Trail from Kabeyun Trail/Talus Lake Trail and hoped someone who had already hiked it could confirm if there are any water sources on the way that can be accessed to filter water. Thanks,

Long hike in but it is relatively flat compared to the chest. Once reaching the top of the giant trail head you pass a really nice lake. The trail starts to become pretty strenuous as the trail begins to zig zag it’s way up the cliff side. The hike offers amazing views!!  One thing I noticed upon reaching the top is that you need to continue hiking until you find the chimney chute route which climbs between two massive cliffs. There is not a lot of trail markers at the top to direct you but don’t get discouraged.

Just did this hike with my son yesterday and the view from the top was spectacular! The hike was moderate for part of the way and then became difficult for the last 4K climb to the top. 100% worth every sore muscle I have today!
Wonderful reward for the effort in the hike. The views from the Knees of the Giant are breathtaking!!

Weather was right around 10 degC with slight wind which kept the hike a little chilly. The entire hike with rest time took us around 9 Hours.

We did couple of short breaks on the way up, and just one break on the way down. Started hiking at 9 AM, visited sea lion which is a left at 0.7 km mark. Rejoining the trail after Sea lion, we proceeded till almost 4km mark. Access to a restroom and a nice scenic view from the shoreline. Then, Tee harbor was the next stop for a quick snack at 5.8km mark. 
Next right at 8KM mark points to the Talus Lake. 1 KM into the Talus Lake  trail, take the deviation to left for Top of the Gaint. The round trip to Top of Gaint and back to this point is 6 Kms.
Excellent view, decent day hike!
Beautiful views once you are at the top. Tough ascent and descent.

Absolutely amazing hike. Lots of vistas to stop and admire the view from, and the final vista is amazing. Beautiful lake as well before ascending the Giant, where we saw Common Goldeneye ducks with babies. The first 8 km are very flat--after that it's a steep, yet challenging and rewarding climb. Highly recommend.

Great all day hike with rewarding view!  If you plan well and start early, this trail is rewarding enough for kids. I brought mine, ages 10, 8, and just 6.  Up to this hike they had not been over 10 miles in a day so we brought hybrid bikes to pedal the Kabeyun portion of the trail(about 7.5km).  Kabeyun is a fairly flat trail with some rocks and tree roots to navigate around and quite wide so very comfortable for  a young cyclist.  At the base of the Top of Giant trail there is a bike rack that can hold 12 bikes.  We locked ours as did the other couple that used the rack.  Trail up is steep but isn't long enough to make kids complain too much and there are a few views through the trees for entertainment.  View from the top is worth the hike for kids. We saw no other kids on the trail that day.  Tea Harbor makes a great pit stop on the return as well and is a fairly private backcountry campsite with a sandy beach.
